## Historical implementation and proposals

The [compiler design and source-layout archive](history/compiler.qmd) preserves compiler migration records and source-layout contracts with provenance. The [program and campaign archive](history/programs.qmd) preserves dated program plans, contracts, audits, and evidence narratives under purpose-based names. The [2026-10-28 implementation snapshot](https://github.com/tumlinso/Cellerator/blob/main/docs/history/current_implementation_2026-10-28.qmd) retains detailed dated capability and experiment notes. Its historical entry includes a correction pointing to the final prepared-routing receipt. The [CelleraTorch archive](history/celleratorch.qmd) preserves the earlier component implementation notes and source snapshot alongside the later paused runtime proposal. The paused proposal did not implement a package; the earlier component source remains historical material outside the current installed API.

The [legacy plan archive](https://github.com/tumlinso/Cellerator/blob/main/planning/archive/legacy-plans/README.md) preserves the former root plan JSONs. The [repository-note archive](https://github.com/tumlinso/Cellerator/blob/main/docs/history/repository-notes/README.md) preserves older root architecture, optimization, migration and environment notes, former guide pointers, and historical assertion source. Both indexes resolve former paths and record exact content identities. These archives are historical context; the maintained chapters above remain the current reading route.

The [legacy Todo archive index](https://github.com/tumlinso/Cellerator/blob/main/planning/archive/legacy-todo/README.md) resolves archived projections, snapshots, plan inputs and runtime artifacts by former path. The current `.todo-orchestrator/project.json` and authority database remain live workflow state. Branch-preservation records remain with their project-control owners and are not duplicated here. Original source-bound reports and receipts remain unchanged; use their recorded source, workload, and validation boundaries when interpreting results.
